samples.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small window drawn with a thick grey frame. Every mark outside that frame, grey or coloured or black, is inert decoration and changes nothing. Inside the window stand four equally wide columns of equal total height, side by side. Each column is filled from its floor upward with one solid colour, red, blue, green or purple, and the pale grey part above the fill is empty: the height of the coloured fill is that pin's size, and the four colours are all different. Below the columns lies a short stack of solid black brackets. Each bracket spans exactly two neighbouring columns and means: compare those two pins and move the taller pin into the left one of the two columns and the shorter pin into the right one, carrying each pin's colour and its fill height together; if the pin already in the left column is at least as tall, nothing moves. Apply the brackets one at a time in top-to-bottom order, and let each bracket act on the arrangement left behind by the brackets above it. The small solid black square above the columns marks the one column to read at the end. After every bracket has been applied in top-to-bottom order, what colour is the pin standing in the marked column? Answer with one of red, blue, green or purple.
